summary.en: Israel continues airstrikes on southern Lebanese towns such as Aita al-Jabal, Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and the Marjayoun Plain, while Hezbollah artillery fires back at Israeli positions. Hezbollah has begun distributing aid, announcing its first payment to war victims and displaced families and pledging further assistance to those uprooted by the conflict. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon due to the fighting. Damage assessments note that Israeli shelling has affected roughly a quarter of Lebanon's agricultural land, worsening the humanitarian situation.
summary.nb: Israel fortsetter luftangrep på sørlige libanesiske byer som Aita al-Jabal, Zawtar al-Sharqiyah og Marjayoun-plainen, mens Hizbollahs artilleri skyter tilbake mot israelske posisjoner. Hizbollah har begynt å distribuere hjelp, kunngjort sin første utbetaling til krigsrammede og fordrevne familier og lovet ytterligere bistand til de som er tvunget på flukt av konflikten. FN rapporterer at 300 000 personer er fordrevet i Libanon på grunn av kampene. Skadevurderinger viser at israelsk bombardement har berørt omtrent en fjerdedel av Libanons landbruksareal, noe som forverrer den humanitære situasjonen.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
